messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — scheduling a short control-plane + cache refresh on Thu 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (2h window). This is a rolling change across control-plane nodes and the prefix/KV cache refresh. Expected impact: brief token-latency spikes (approx 5-15s) for a small percentage of in-flight requests during node restart; no database migrations or schema changes.

maria: Ops asks: please have an on-call primary for 02:00-04:00 UTC, follow the standard handoff checklist, and post the statuspage + customer notice 1 hour before start. Incident bot will escalate if >5m of sustained 5xx or >30% of requests exceed latency threshold.

statusbot: Draft status page entry (please review):
- Component: Control Plane / Cache Refresh
- Start: 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC
- ETA: 2026-04-02 04:00 UTC
- Impact: Brief intermittent latency spikes (5-15s) for a subset of API requests during rolling restarts. No expected data loss.
- Update cadence: every 30m or on meaningful change.

jon: ack — I'll take primary for that window. I'll be paged for pager severity >= P2. I'll watch error-rate (5xx) and median p95 token latency.

kevin: Thanks @jon. Mitigation notes for oncall:
- If we see node-level OOMs, drain affected serving nodes: `redwoodctl nodes drain --node <node-id> --grace 30s`
- Temporarily route traffic away from region if error rate sustained: `rwctl route set --region eu-west1 --weight 0.2` (roll back with `--weight 1.0`)
- Healthcheck: `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.example/v1/health | head -n 20`
- If token-latency spike correlates with cache warmup, enable aggressive prefix cache for hot keys: see runbook section "cache-warmup".

kevin: PS — set the alert silence for non-actionable latency blips under 20s in the next 2 hours to avoid repeated noisy pages: `incbot silence add --alert latency-p95 --duration 30m`

eve: Can someone paste a short customer-facing blurb for support to use if users ask? Need one for email and one for the status page short summary.

maria: Customer-facing short (status page):
"Scheduled maintenance: We will perform a rolling control-plane refresh on Thu 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. You may experience brief latency spikes for a minority of requests. No action required. We will post updates here."

maria: Customer-facing email template (support):
"Hello —
We’re performing scheduled maintenance on Thu 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (2h window). During this time some API requests may see short latency increases (typically <15s). There should be no service interruption or data loss. If you experience sustained errors, please reply to this thread and we’ll investigate immediately.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference"

deploy-bot: Scheduled job queued: `controlplane-refresh-20260402` — ETA 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Job id: cpr-20260402-73a

jon: Preparing handoff notes: I'll be oncall remotely from 01:50 UTC. Pager rules + runbooks are bookmarked. If anything looks off, escalate to kevin and then to maria.

statusbot: Status page set to "Maintenance scheduled" and a short banner posted. Reminder: update at 02:30 and on completion.

(02:00 UTC) deploy-bot: Rollout started — control-plane nodes will be refreshed in batches (batch size = 3 nodes). Tracking job: cpr-20260402-73a

(02:07 UTC) jon: Noticing a small p95 spike in the control-plane token path; 5xx remains flat. Looks like cache warmup. Applying temporary route shift to reduce tail latency.

(02:12 UTC) kevin: Observed cache priming pattern. Incrementally bumping cache prefill for top prefixes. No customer-facing errors.

(02:35 UTC) statusbot: Update: Rolling refresh in progress. Intermittent latency spikes observed, no sustained errors or increased 5xx rates. Next update 03:05 UTC or earlier if status changes.

(03:50 UTC) deploy-bot: Rollout completed for all targeted control-plane nodes. Job cpr-20260402-73a -> success

(03:53 UTC) jon: Confirmed latency profile back to baseline for all regions. No alerts fired during last 30m. I'm closing the handoff once final checks pass.

(03:58 UTC) statusbot: Status updated to "Maintenance complete" with summary: rolling refresh completed; brief latency spikes observed but no customer-impacting errors; full service restored.

maria: Thanks team — posting completion note to customer channels. If any customers report sustained issues, route them to support and ping me. :tada:

(04:00 UTC) jon: Handoff complete — primary cleared. Closing thread.
